adaptation_telemetry.application_rule: Commit after publication of source frame; first eligible use is next input. Final-frame update has no subsequent input in this experiment.

limitations: One known synthetic development sequence, correlated frames, not held out and not proof of physical instance recovery.
All thresholds and populations retained; abstention is not success and zero-publication risk is null.
Author host reuses frozen metric formulas; CPU contracts are not independent geometric verification.
Accepted head updates, losses and native output changes are telemetry, not GT performance.
Both runs cover 180 inputs; instrumented and uncontrolled timing does not establish deployment FPS or a causal speed gain.
The three phase boundaries are inherited input-condition boundaries, fixed before reading new GPU output or GT.
An ADD candidate improvement does not establish gains for MSSD, MSPD, published availability or physical instance identity. Correct rejected candidates can increase.
Instrumented tracking time includes current gates, surface rendering, gradients and full evidence retention. It is not deployment FPS or an isolated training cost.
Update/commit time was not separately instrumented and is null; no inferred update time is fabricated.
Shadow updated tensors and per-parameter gradients were not persisted; proposed losses remain source-verified telemetry.
